work_order.confidence_rationale: Every change is in one file read end to end; the two handler call sites are both on the page inspected; the tab order AC-3 now checks has been derived from the markup this plan specifies (back control at :74, tabindex="-1" heading at :75, first expense field at :79) and is stated identically in the plan, the criterion and the qa script, so the contradiction the last review found cannot recur. The fallback in AC-11 is now covered by a named test case rather than asserted of a browser session. The remaining uncertainty is behavioural and belongs to QA: exact focus-ring rendering per browser, and how a screen reader reads '← Back to groups'. Neither can change the shape of the diff.
work_order.understanding: The app's entire navigation is two click handlers on elements the keyboard cannot reach. public/index.html:74 is a <span id="back-link"> carrying a click listener (:570) — not a link, not a button, not focusable, so it never receives focus and Enter and Space do nothing on it. public/index.html:197-201 renders every group as an <li> with a click listener, so the list of groups cannot be tabbed to or announced as a list of things to activate. Nothing in the stylesheet (:7-53) defines a :focus or outline rule, so the controls that ARE natively focusable carry only the browser default ring, sitting next to a `button { border: none }` rule at :16 that removes the border the default ring is drawn against. I confirmed all four claims against the file on the current branch. Three facts shape the fix and are load-bearing for the acceptance criteria: the ids #back-link, #group-list and #group-title need not change at all; the settlement Mark done path is already a real <button> with a delegated listener, so it is untouched; and the group's DOM order is fixed — the back control (:74), then the heading (:75), then the first expense field #expense-desc (:79) — which is the order AC-3 is now written against.
work_order.root_cause: The navigation was built as behaviour attached to presentation elements — a span and an li that answer a click. An element that only responds to pointer input is not in the accessibility tree's set of operable controls: it takes no focus, has no role, and no key event reaches it. Nothing about the markup or the stylesheet was ever asked to be operable this way, so nothing failed loudly; the app works perfectly for a mouse. The stylesheet's lack of a focus rule is the second half of the same defect: even the natively focusable controls announce their position only through a browser default that the `button { border: none }` rule at :16 undercuts.
work_order.approach:
Make the two navigation controls real controls and give the whole page a focus indicator this repository draws itself, keeping every id and class that .sdlc/memory/qa/selectors.md documents. Six edits, all in public/index.html. (1) The back control becomes `<button type="button" class="back-link" id="back-link">` — same text, same class, same id, so it keeps its documented selector and its appearance, and it gains Enter and Space activation natively with no key handler at all. (2) Each group row keeps its <li> so the list is still a list, and gains a <button class="group-item" data-group-id="…"> inside it, carrying the group name as its text content so its accessible name is the name and the existing stored-XSS posture is unchanged. (3) A `:focus-visible` rule draws a 3px solid #1d4ed8 ring at 2px offset — 6.7:1 on white, 6.2:1 on the #f5f5f5 body, well past the 3:1 a non-text indicator needs. `:focus-visible` and not `:focus`, deliberately: a ring that follows the mouse nags everyone who did not ask for one. (4) Escape returns to the group list from anywhere in the group view, including from inside a text field, and does nothing on the create view where there is nowhere to go back to. (5) Focus is managed on both transitions: opening a group focuses #group-title (given tabindex="-1", which does not put it in the Tab order) only after the fetch resolves, so the name is announced rather than a placeholder; leaving restores focus to the row the user came from, matched by group id, with a three-way fallback to the first row and then to #group-name. The group list is rebuilt on every load, so the restore is a lookup by id, not a retained element. (6) The heading gets a 'Loading…' placeholder so the view is never on screen with an empty h1.

THE TAB ORDER, stated once and used by AC-3 and by the qa script. The markup is not reordered. In the group view the tabbable sequence is: the back control (:74), then #expense-desc (:79), #expense-amount, #expense-payer, the two split-mode radios, the split checkboxes, the Add Expense submit, and the Mark done buttons. The heading at :75 carries tabindex="-1" and is therefore never a Tab stop. Two consequences follow, and both acceptance criteria are written from them rather than from a wish: (a) focus after opening a group is ON the heading, so pressing Tab there moves FORWARD past it to #expense-desc — the back control is not reachable by Tab from the heading; (b) the back control is the stop immediately BEFORE the description field, so it is reached with Shift+Tab from #expense-desc. AC-3 checks (b) and says so explicitly. The other view is display:none (`.hidden` at :36) while this one is on screen, so no tab stop wraps around between them.

Two CSS traps, both because `button:hover` is specificity 0,1,1 and outranks a bare class: the base button rule would paint the back control a solid indigo block on hover, and the group row the same. Both are cancelled with explicit `:hover` rules rather than by reordering, so the outcome does not depend on where the rules sit in the file.

The padding moves from the li onto the button so the whole card is the hit area rather than a text-only target inside a padded card; rendered size is unchanged. The settlement panel, the balances panel, the expense list, the create-group form and document.title are all left alone — Mark done is the one path in this app that moves money, and it is already a real button, so the change is confined to navigation.

files.why: The back control, the group rows, the heading and the stylesheet all live in this one static file — the repo is one node process and one static page by design (ADR-0001, conventions.md). Every change named in the ticket is in here and nowhere else.

cases: the back control is a real control, not a span: read public/index.html from disk, collapse runs of whitespace, assert the markup matches /<button[^>]*\bid="back-link"/, and assert it does NOT match /<span[^>]*\bid="back-link"/ nor /<a(?![^>]*\bhref)[^>]*\bid="back-link"/ — the id is deliberately unchanged so the documented #back-link selector keeps resolving

the same control is what the server actually serves: boot the server with start({ port: 0, store: createStore({ memory: true }) }) from src/server.js, GET "/" and assert status 200, that Content-Type starts with "text/html", and that the response body contains the button form of the back control. src/server.js caches index.html in htmlCache (:18-25), so this is the markup a browser receives, not just the file on disk

the group list builds one button per group and no longer a listener on the li: slice the inline <script> out of public/index.html, assert it does NOT match /li.addEventListener('click'/ anywhere, and DOES match each of /button.className = 'group-item'/, /button.dataset.groupId = group.id/, /button.textContent = group.name/, /button.type = 'button'/ and /button.addEventListener('click', \(\) => showGroupView\(group.id\)\)/ — this is the assertion that the whole of the app's navigation stopped being mouse-only

the group row's accessible name is the group name and is set as text: assert the render loop assigns button.textContent = group.name, and that the slice of the script from 'for (const group of data.groups)' to the end of that loop contains no innerHTML — the row must not become the stored-XSS sink that test/xss.test.js already guards elsewhere in this file

the stylesheet defines a focus indicator of its own: slice everything between <style> and </style>, assert it matches /:focus-visibles*{[^}]*outline:s*3px solid #1d4ed8/ and /:focus-visibles*{[^}]*outline-offset:s*2px/, and assert it does NOT match /outline:s*(none|0)/ anywhere in the block — a rule that cancels the ring is the regression this case exists to catch

the back control's hover fill is cancelled, so the base button rule does not repaint it: assert the <style> block matches /.back-link:hovers*{[^}]*background:s*none/ — button:hover is specificity 0,1,1 and outranks .back-link at 0,1,0, so without this the back control becomes a solid indigo block under the pointer

the group row's hover fill is cancelled for the same reason, and the row is still a full-width target: assert the <style> block matches /.group-list button:hovers*{[^}]*background:s*none/ and that the .group-list button rule sets /width:s*100%/

the tab order AC-3 depends on is the one the markup actually has, and nothing was reordered to suit the test: index the back control, the <h1 id="group-title"> and id="expense-desc" in the markup and assert back < group-title < expense-desc in document order, that the h1 carries tabindex="-1", and that the h1 element's tagName is H1 — the heading is skipped by Tab, which is why AC-3 reaches the back control with Shift+Tab from #expense-desc and not with Tab from the heading. A refactor that moved the back control below the heading would fail here rather than silently breaking QA

Escape returns to the group list, and only from the group list: read the inline <script>, assert it matches /document.addEventListener('keydown'/, then slice from that index to the next "\n});" and assert the slice tests e.key !== 'Escape', asserts that #view-group carries the hidden class, and calls showCreateView()

the back control still works by click and needs no key path of its own: assert the <script> still matches /getElementById\('back-link'\).addEventListener\('click', showCreateView\);/ exactly — one handler, with Enter and Space left to the button itself

focus comes back to the row that was opened, not to the body: assert the <script> declares /let lastOpenedGroupId = null;/, that the showGroupView slice assigns lastOpenedGroupId = groupId, and that the showCreateView slice calls loadGroups() followed by a .then( that reads '#group-list .group-item', compares row.dataset.groupId === lastOpenedGroupId, and calls .focus(). Index the three and assert loadGroups comes first: a focus restore that runs before the list is rebuilt restores focus to nothing

the focus restore falls back to the first row, then to #group-name, when the opened row is not in the rebuilt list: slice showCreateView out of the inline script and assert the target expression is the FULL three-arm chain, in order — rows.find((row) => row.dataset.groupId === lastOpenedGroupId), then `|| rows[0]`, then `|| document.getElementById('group-name')` — and that the slice calls .focus() on it. This is the only coverage those arms can have: src/server.js has no delete route and the page exposes no delete control, so no browser session can produce a group that has gone missing. AC-11 says so rather than leaving the clause looking browser-checked

opening a group focuses its heading, and only after the name is in it: assert the markup contains <h1 id="group-title" tabindex="-1">, that the showGroupView slice sets the group-title textContent to the placeholder, and that within that slice loadGroup( appears before group-title').focus() — the ordering is the assertion, because focusing on the placeholder reads out 'Loading' instead of the group name

the settlement money path is untouched: assert the <script> still matches /getElementById\('settlement-list'\).addEventListener\('click'/, /button.className = 'transfer-done-btn'/ and /button.dataset.amount = String\(transfer.amountPaise\)/ — the delegated listener, the class and the dataset the Mark done handler reads must all survive this change untouched

every selector documented in .sdlc/memory/qa/selectors.md still resolves in the served page: GET "/" from a booted server and assert the body contains each of #view-create-group, #view-group, create-group-form, #group-name, #group-members, #create-group-error, #group-list, #back-link, #group-title, #expense-form, #expense-desc, #expense-amount, #expense-payer, name="split-mode", #split-checkboxes, #expense-error, #balances-panel, #balances-error, #balances-list, #settlement-panel, #settlement-error, #settlement-list and #expense-list. This is what discharges the ticket's 'selectors are updated' requirement without editing the reserved memory file. Note that .transfer-done-btn, .panel-list, .empty-state and .share-input are created at runtime by the script and are asserted in the other cases, not here

acceptance.check: On the group list, pressing Tab moves focus through every group row; the focused element is a BUTTON carrying the class group-item, and the focused row is visibly marked (its card background changes and a ring is drawn just outside it).
acceptance.how_to_verify: Open http://localhost:3000/ with the seed group present. Press Tab from the top of the page until focus lands on a group row. In devtools, confirm document.activeElement.tagName === "BUTTON" and its classList contains group-item.

acceptance.check: With a group row focused, pressing Enter opens that group, and pressing Space does the same; the group view appears with #group-title reading the group name.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Tab to a group row, press Enter, confirm #view-group is no longer .hidden and #group-title textContent is the group name. Press Back to groups, Tab to the row again, press Space and confirm the same.

acceptance.check: In the group view the back control is the tab stop immediately BEFORE the expense fields: with focus on #expense-desc, pressing Shift+Tab moves focus to it, and Enter or Space on it returns to the group list. The back control is NOT the next Tab stop after a group opens — opening a group leaves focus on the heading (AC-6), and the heading carries tabindex="-1", so Tab from there moves forward past it to #expense-desc. The DOM order is back control, then heading (skipped by Tab), then #expense-desc, and this criterion is derived from exactly that order.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Open a group and wait until document.activeElement.id === "group-title" (that is AC-6 landing; the group view's controls are inert-ish until the load resolves). Press Tab once: focus should move FORWARD to #expense-desc, because the tabindex="-1" heading is not a Tab stop. Press Shift+Tab once: focus must land on the back control — confirm document.activeElement.id === "back-link" and its tagName is BUTTON. Press Enter on it and confirm #view-create-group is no longer .hidden. If a browser restarts Shift+Tab from the top of the document instead of from the previous stop, that is the browser's behaviour and not this app's: use the same check from the create-view side — Tab to the Create Group button, then Tab forward until the group row, and confirm the row is reachable — or re-run in Chrome. The criterion that must hold in every browser is the one stated first: from #expense-desc, Shift+Tab lands on the back control.

acceptance.check: Pressing Escape anywhere in the group view, including inside the description and amount fields, returns to the group list. Escape on the create-group view does nothing.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Open a group, click into #expense-desc so focus is in a text field, press Escape, confirm the create view is showing. Then press Escape again and confirm nothing changes.

acceptance.check: After leaving the group view by either route — Escape or the back control — focus lands on the group-item button of the group that was open, matched by its dataset.groupId, and not on <body>. The fallback for a group that is no longer in the list is a separate criterion (AC-11) because no browser session can reach that state.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Open the seeded Goa trip group, press Escape, then WAIT for the group list to rebuild before reading focus — showCreateView() re-fetches GET /api/groups and focuses the row inside the .then(), so for a moment after the keypress document.activeElement is <body>. Poll document.activeElement until it is not <body> (or wait ~200ms), then confirm document.activeElement.classList contains group-item and its dataset.groupId is "seed-goa". Repeat using the back control instead of Escape. Also confirm this is a match by id, not by luck of ordering: open group A, go back, open group B, go back, and confirm focus follows to the B row each time.

acceptance.check: On opening a group, #group-title is focused and its text is the group name — never empty, and never still reading the loading placeholder by the time focus settles.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Open a group from the list and, in devtools, confirm document.activeElement.id === "group-title" and its textContent is the group name. Repeat for a second group so the previous group name cannot be mistaken for the current one. Note that this is also why AC-3 uses Shift+Tab: Tab from the heading moves forward to the description field.

acceptance.check: After pressing Tab, the focused control shows a 3px solid indigo focus indicator drawn by the app stylesheet, visible against both the white card it sits on and the grey page behind it.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Tab to a group row, the back control and a form input in turn. In devtools, read getComputedStyle(document.activeElement) and confirm outlineStyle is "solid", outlineWidth is "3px" and outlineColor is rgb(29, 78, 216). The ring must also be visible on screen by eye — the browser default ring alone does not satisfy this, since the base button rule removes the border it was drawn against. Shift+Tab counts: :focus-visible matches on either key.

acceptance.check: The hover and focus restyling of the two navigational controls did not change their appearance: the back control is still blue text with an underline on hover, not a filled indigo block, and a group row is still a white card that greys under the pointer.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Hover the back control and a group row in the browser. The back control must stay blue-on-white with an underline; the group row card must turn #e5e7eb, not #1d4ed8.

acceptance.check: The money path is unaffected: a pending settlement can still be marked done by clicking its Mark done button, the row becomes .transfer-done with a strike-through, and the balances update.
acceptance.how_to_verify: On the seeded group, click Mark done on a pending transfer, confirm the row gains the transfer-done class and the balances panel re-renders. Then reload the page and confirm the settlement is still recorded.

acceptance.check: Every selector documented in .sdlc/memory/qa/selectors.md still resolves in the served page, so the browser test in #19 drives the real elements when it is unblocked.
acceptance.how_to_verify: In devtools on the served page, run document.querySelector for each documented selector: #back-link, #group-list, #group-title, #view-group, #view-create-group, #create-group-form, #group-name, #group-members, #create-group-error, #expense-form, #expense-desc, #expense-amount, #expense-payer, #split-checkboxes, #expense-error, #balances-panel, #balances-error, #balances-list, #settlement-panel, #settlement-error, #settlement-list, #expense-list. All must return an element.

acceptance.check: When the row a group was opened from is not present in the rebuilt list, the focus restore falls back to the first row, and with no rows at all to the group-name input, rather than leaving focus on <body>.
acceptance.how_to_verify: NOT a browser check, and deliberately so: src/server.js serves index, healthz, groups (GET/POST), group_balances, group_settlement, group_settlements (POST) and group_expenses (GET/POST) and has no delete route — every method-rejection branch in it is a METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED 405 (index :123, healthz :129, and :182, :202, :231, :283, :352) — and public/index.html exposes no delete control either, so no browser session can produce a group that has stopped existing. The arms are defensive and are covered instead by the test case in test/a11y-navigation.test.js named "the focus restore falls back to the first row, then to #group-name, when the opened row is not in the rebuilt list", which asserts the full `|| rows[0] || document.getElementById('group-name')` chain is present in showCreateView and that .focus() is called on its result. QA: run `node --test test/` and read that case, not the page.

qa_script: Bring the app up: `node bin/seed.js && node src/server.js`, then open http://localhost:3000/.
Open devtools on the page first — several checks below are read off document.activeElement and getComputedStyle, and clicking through first will change what :focus-visible matches.

Tab from the top of the page. Confirm the first stop after the form is the Create Group button and that the group row that follows is a BUTTON with class group-item. A row that only reacts to clicks, or a focus ring that never appears, is a fail.
With a group row focused, press Enter. Confirm the group view opened and #group-title reads "Goa trip". Go back, focus a row again, press Space, and confirm the same thing happens.

Open a group and WAIT until document.activeElement.id is "group-title" — opening a group leaves focus on the heading, not on the back control. The heading is tabindex="-1", so pressing Tab from it moves FORWARD past it: Tab once should land on the Description field (#expense-desc). That is correct, not a bug. The back control is the stop BEFORE the description field, so press Shift+Tab from there: focus must land on it (a BUTTON, id back-link), and Enter on it must return you to the group list. Do not expect the back control to be the next Tab stop after opening a group — the DOM order is back control, heading, description field, and only the heading is skipped by Tab. AC-3 checks exactly this direction.
Open the group again, click into the Description field, and press Escape. Confirm the group list is showing. Press Escape again on the list and confirm nothing changes.

With a group open, press Escape and then WAIT for the list to rebuild before reading focus — showCreateView() re-fetches GET /api/groups and focuses the row inside the .then(), so document.activeElement is <body> for a moment after the keypress. Poll it in devtools (`(()=>{const t=setInterval(()=>{if(document.activeElement!==document.body){clearInterval(t);console.log(document.activeElement.className, document.activeElement.dataset.groupId)}},50)})()`) until it reports the group-item button for "Goa trip" and dataset.groupId "seed-goa". <body> forever is a fail. Repeat the same check using the back control rather than Escape.

Open group A, then go back, then open group B, then go back — after each rebuild, confirm focus follows to the row of the group that was just open, not always to the first row. This is what proves the restore matches by dataset.groupId rather than by position.
Open a group and read document.activeElement.id: it must be group-title, and its textContent must be the group name, not empty and not "Loading…".

Tab through at least: a group row, the back control, #group-name, #expense-desc, the split-mode radios, a split checkbox, and the Mark done button. Read getComputedStyle(document.activeElement) for each — outlineStyle "solid", outlineWidth "3px", outlineColor rgb(29, 78, 216). Shift+Tab counts the same as Tab here.
Hover the back control and a group row. Neither may turn into a filled indigo block; the row card must grey to #e5e7eb and the back control must underline.

Regression on the money path: on the seeded group, click Mark done on a pending transfer. Confirm the row strikes through, gains .transfer-done, and the balances change. Reload and confirm it is still recorded.
Run document.querySelector for every selector listed in .sdlc/memory/qa/selectors.md and confirm each returns an element (AC-10).

AC-11 is the one criterion with no browser step: nothing in this app deletes a group, so the fallback arms are unreachable by clicking. Read it with `node --test test/` instead — run the suite and confirm the case named in AC-11's how_to_verify passes.
risks: The ticket asks for `.sdlc/memory/qa/selectors.md` to be updated. That file cannot be in files[]: `check-forbidden.mjs` runs with --reject at the plan stage and `reservedRules()` adds `.sdlc/memory/**` for any branch that is not the Librarian's or the project planner's, so naming it would get this entire work order refused unread. The requirement is met instead by not needing the edit — the change keeps #back-link, #group-list and #group-title exactly as they are, and test/a11y-navigation.test.js's last case plus AC-10 assert that every selector in that file still resolves against the served page. What genuinely changed is two ADDITIONS (`.group-item` and `[data-group-id]`) for elements that did not exist before; recording those in the selectors file is a Librarian follow-up on the memory stage, not this ticket. Flagging it here so nobody is surprised when that file is not in the diff.

Regression is the real risk, and it is concentrated in QA selectors: the group rows are new elements, so anything selecting `#group-list li` and reading its text still works (the li wraps the button and the text is one level down, so a direct `li.textContent` read now returns the same string) but anything asserting on the row element itself — class, dataset, focus — is new surface. AC-10 walks the documented selector list so this is checked rather than assumed.

The :focus-visible ring is a keyboard affordance and is deliberately NOT shown on a plain mouse press. QA checking the outline after clicking, rather than after pressing Tab or Shift+Tab, will see none. AC-7 and the qa_script both say Tab explicitly for this reason, and approach states it as a decision rather than leaving it to be discovered.

The `Loading…` placeholder is a judgement call: the alternative was leaving the h1 empty until the fetch resolves, which is what happens today. On a failed load the heading keeps saying Loading…, which is not true — the group view's error state is explicitly out of scope per the ticket, and this is strictly better than the empty heading, not correct. Noted so nobody reads the placeholder as a claim that the view handles load failure.

The `.catch(() => {})` on the two focus chains suppresses a failure that would otherwise surface as an unhandled rejection. It is not new error handling: loadGroups() was already called unawaited from the initial load (:573) with no catch, and loadGroup() already had the same shape. The chain is added only because .focus() has to run afterwards.
No host is added. The change makes no new outbound request; `env.api_allowlist` in .sdlc/config.yml is empty and stays correct, because this ticket adds no call to anything outside the app.
Zero dependencies added, so ADR-0001 and the sdlc:verify contract (node --test) are untouched.
residual_risks: AC-3 depends on the browser implementing sequential focus navigation the way Chrome and Firefox do today: Shift+Tab from #expense-desc goes to the previous tabbable stop, which is the back control. Firefox's older habit of restarting from the top of the document on Shift+Tab would fail the check. The criterion's how_to_verify says what to do in that case (verify the forward direction on the create view instead, or re-run in Chrome) rather than leaving a browser-dependent failure unexplained — but it is a real dependency, not a hypothetical one, and it is a property of the browser rather than of this diff.

The focus restore in AC-5 depends on a network round trip. On a slow connection the gap between the keypress and focus landing can be a second or more, and any tester who reads document.activeElement immediately will see <body> and report a false failure. Both the criterion and the qa script say to wait and give the polling snippet; that is a documentation fix, not a code one.

The three-arm focus fallback (AC-11) is not reachable by any user action in this app. It is covered by a string assertion on the source, not by executing the code path: a test that passes does not prove the fallback behaves correctly at runtime, only that it is written the way this plan specifies. If a delete route is ever added, that clause needs a real test.
out_of_scope: `.sdlc/memory/qa/selectors.md` — reserved path, the guard refuses the whole plan for it. See risks: the requirement is discharged by keeping every documented selector valid instead.
The two new selectors this change introduces (`.group-item`, `[data-group-id]`) being written into that file. A Librarian follow-up, because .sdlc/memory/** is the memory stage's to write.
The settlement panel, the balances panel, and the expense list beyond the group heading — the ticket's own scope line, and the one place where a careless diff would reach the money path.

A delete path for a group, or any change to src/server.js. AC-11's fallback stays defensive because adding the route that would exercise it is a different ticket with a data-retention decision attached.

Colour contrast, font sizes, and the *Experience* section of docs/spec/tabs.md about loading and error states. The focus ring is the one contrast-adjacent thing this touches, and only because an indicator has to be visible to count as one.

Any dependency, framework, or build change. The repo is Node 20 standard library and one static file, and it stays that way — the whole test suite for this ticket is node:test and string assertions against the served markup, with no browser driver, which is what lets it run now rather than waiting on #19.
docs/spec/tabs.md — a protected doc, and the spec is not this ticket to amend.

The create-group form's own focus order, its error announcements, and the share-input error line. The controls there are natively focusable already, so nothing about them is broken; wiring the error line to the error message with aria-describedby is a separate ticket and would widen this one.

document.title. The ticket asks that the view title be announced; focusing #group-title after the name is in it does that. Changing the browser tab title is a separate product decision, not a keyboard fix.

Skip links, landmark elements (`<main>`, `<nav>`), and heading-level reordering across the two views. The two h1s are already one-per-view and the hidden view is display:none so it is out of the accessibility tree; a landmark audit is real work and is not what this ticket found.

alternatives_considered.approach: Drop the heading-focus step from showGroupView so that a single Tab after opening a group lands on the back control, and restate AC-6 accordingly.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It answers the review's objection by making the app worse to hit the criterion rather than by fixing the criterion. The heading is the view's title and focusing it is what announces the group's name, which the ticket asks for explicitly; without it a keyboard user opens a group and lands on a bare text field with no idea which group they are in. The review offered this as one of two ways out and required the cost to be paid in a restated AC-6 — not taken, because the other way out costs nothing and keeps both behaviours.

alternatives_considered.approach: Move the back control below the <h1> in the markup so the heading comes first in DOM order and Tab reaches the back control next.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It inverts reading order to serve a keystroke: the control that returns you to the list would come after the title it belongs to, and it would change the visual order of the page for every user, mouse included. The review noted this is a plan change rather than an implementer's choice — it is that, and the plan declines it.

alternatives_considered.approach: Drop the two fallback arms in showCreateView and the second sentence of AC-5, since no browser session can reach them.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The other half of the review's required action, and the weaker one. Trimming defensive code so a clause becomes untestable inverts the priority: the arms cost two `||` and stop a future focus-restore from dumping focus on <body> if a delete route ever lands, whereas keeping them costs one named test case. Kept, and covered.

alternatives_considered.approach: Put the .sdlc/memory/qa/selectors.md edit in files[] as the ticket literally asks, and let the reserved-path guard refuse the plan.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: check-forbidden.mjs runs at the plan stage with --reject and drops the whole work order, costing a full replan to learn a rule the guard would have refused for anyway — and the guard message itself says to plan the change without it and name it in risks. Resolved by keeping the selectors valid instead, which satisfies the requirement the bullet was reaching for.

alternatives_considered.approach: Make the back control an `<a href="#view-create-group">` and leave it to the browser to do the navigation.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It changes the URL, needs a click handler to stop the hash change from firing, and adds a history entry the user then has to press Back through — in exchange for nothing a button does not do. A link with no href is worse: it is not focusable, which is the defect being fixed.

alternatives_considered.approach: Add a keydown handler on the existing span and li so Enter and Space fire the click, leaving the elements as they are.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It fixes the symptom and leaves the cause: the controls would still have no role, would still be absent from the set of things a screen reader offers to activate, and would still be invisible to a browser's own focus handling. The issue asks for the right element for the job and this is the wrong element with a key handler stapled on.

alternatives_considered.approach: Replace the whole li with a bare button, dropping the list wrapper.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It loses the list semantics the ticket explicitly wants preserved — a screen reader announcing a list of things to activate — and breaks the existing `.group-list li` card styling that both the hover and the focus-within treatment build on.

alternatives_considered.approach: Use `:focus` instead of `:focus-visible` for the ring.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Every mouse click would leave a ring on the control the user just used, including the Mark done button that disables itself. The indicator is for people who cannot see where they are; showing it to people who just clicked is noise.

alternatives_considered.approach: Make Escape a no-op while focus is inside the description or amount fields, so a stray Escape never discards a half-typed expense.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It adds a conditional nobody asked for, and the state it protects is not lost — the form keeps its values across the view toggle, so returning restores what was typed. One Escape rule, stated once, is easier to predict than a rule with an exception.

assumptions: The elements this change preserves — #back-link, #group-list, #group-title, .group-list, .empty-state, and the settlement/balances panels — are the ones .sdlc/memory/qa/selectors.md documents as of the current branch, and no other file in the repo selects on the markup being replaced. I grepped src/ and test/ for the ids and for `li.addEventListener`: the only listener of that shape is the one being replaced, and the selectors are read from memory rather than from code.
`node --test` picks up a new file named test/*.test.js without a manifest change. Consistent with the four existing suites and package.json's sdlc:verify; no package.json edit is planned.

QA runs in compose mode against http://localhost:3000 with node bin/seed.js, so the seeded "Goa trip" group (id seed-goa) is on the group list. Several acceptance checks name that id because it is the only stable one available.

Browsers QA uses implement sequential focus navigation as Chrome and Firefox do today: Tab and Shift+Tab move to the next and previous tabbable stop rather than restarting from the top of the document. AC-3 names what to do where that does not hold, and a test case pins the DOM order the criterion depends on so a refactor fails in CI rather than in QA.
unknowns: How the focus ring looks in each browser QA might use. The rule is standard and the colour is specified exactly, but ring rendering on a borderless button is the one visual thing this plan cannot confirm without a browser — hence AC-7 asks for both the computed style and the ring being visible by eye.

Whether a screen reader reads `← Back to groups` better with the arrow hidden from the accessible name. It is left in, as it is today. Worth a follow-up with a real screen reader, not worth guessing at here.
evidence: public/index.html:74 is `← Back to groups` and :570 is its only handler, `document.getElementById('back-link').addEventListener('click', showCreateView);` — a span, so no focus, no Enter, no Space.
public/index.html:197-201 is the group render loop: `li.textContent = group.name; li.addEventListener('click', () => showGroupView(group.id));` — the whole list is mouse-only.
public/index.html:7-53 is the entire <style> block; it contains no :focus and no outline rule, and :16 is `button { ... border: none; ... }` immediately above `button:hover` at :17.

Document order that AC-3 is derived from, read off the current file: back control :74, `<h1 id="group-title">` :75, first expense field `#expense-desc` :79. With the heading given tabindex="-1" it is skipped by Tab, so from the back control Tab reaches #expense-desc and from #expense-desc Shift+Tab reaches the back control. Focus lands on the heading when a group opens (AC-6), so Tab from there moves forward past it. The other view is `.hidden` (:36, display:none) so nothing wraps.

src/server.js has no delete route: it handles index, healthz, groups (GET/POST), group_balances (GET), group_settlement (GET), group_settlements (POST) and group_expenses (GET/POST), and every method-rejection branch in it is a METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED 405 (index :123, healthz :129, and :182, :202, :231, :283, :352) — there is no delete anywhere in it. public/index.html exposes no delete control either — the create view is a form, a list and a submit button (:59-70) and the group view's only mutation is the settlement Mark done handler (:538-567). This is why AC-11 is verify:test and names a tests[] case instead of pretending a browser can reach it.
createGroup refuses a duplicate name, so a group cannot be replaced or shadowed out of the list either — the same reason.

src/server.js:18-25 caches index.html in htmlCache, and test/xss.test.js:31 boots with `start({ port: 0, store })`; test/a11y-navigation.test.js follows that shape so the served-markup assertions test what a browser receives.
work_order.debate_summary: v1 was rejected on two points, both about a criterion that could not be satisfied rather than about the code. Objection 1: AC-3 and qa_script step 4 required a single Tab after opening a group to land on the back control, while the plan's own focus step puts focus on the tabindex="-1" heading at public/index.html:75, which sits between the back control (:74) and #expense-desc (:79) — so Tab moves forward past the heading and AC-3 was unsatisfiable. Resolved by deriving the criterion from the markup rather than moving the markup: the back control stays at :74, AC-3 now checks the direction the order actually produces (from #expense-desc, Shift+Tab lands on the back control, and Enter or Space on it returns to the list), it names where focus is when the tester starts and why Tab from the heading moves the other way, qa_script step 4 says the same thing to a human, and a new test case pins back < heading < #expense-desc in document order so a future reorder fails in CI rather than in QA. Two cheaper fixes were available and declined: dropping the heading-focus step (which answers by removing the announcement of the group name, the thing the ticket asks for) and moving the back control below the heading (which inverts reading order for every user, mouse included) — both are recorded in alternatives_considered. Objection 2: AC-5's clause about a group that no longer exists is unreachable — no delete route, no delete control, and a duplicate name is refused — and nothing in tests[] covered the fallback. Resolved by splitting the clause rather than dropping it: AC-5 now covers only what the browser shows (focus lands on the row that was open, matched by dataset.groupId) and says to wait for the rebuilt list before reading activeElement, because the restore is behind an await of GET /api/groups; the fallback moved to AC-11 with verify "test", which states plainly that no session can reach it and names the test case that does. A new tests[] case asserts the full `|| rows[0] || document.getElementById('group-name')` chain in showCreateView. Everything else in v1 was confirmed against the file and kept.
